findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed multiple cooler units to be 49F. Discussed with PIC, coolers include WIC, the prep cooler to its left, and the standing cooler to the right. Items from the right cooler were actively cooling, wings and meatballs were moved back to walk in freezer. Items in the walk in cooler were probed and ran a temperature of 50F. Items included pizza sauce and pasta, items were discarded. The prep cooler later tested at 41F. Inspector will follow up on 9/4/26. Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F. 

During inspection, Bormida arrived to service coolers. Inspector observed ambient air temperature to begin to drop, inspector will spot check facility on 9/3/26 if completely serviced.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed multiple containers of cut vegetable to be cold holding with no date marking present. Discussed with PIC, vegetables were prepared yesterday (8/22/24). Date marking stickers were placed on vegetables, ensure any TCS food kept longer than 24 hours is properly date marked. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Two locations are observed with cooling TCS foods that do not have indicators for when the cooling process began. Without these it is impossible to know if the cooling process is effective for the items being cooled, especially between shifts. The PIC was consulted and knew approximately when the process began for both items. The gravy in the walk in cooler had a label placed on it and the chicken wings were marked on the dry erase board on their standing cooler intended for this purpose. Ensure that any cooling foods are labeled with their time that the cooling process started. 

3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

The scoop used for the ice machine is stored in a quarter pan. The cardboard flap of a neighboring box is hanging over this location and makes it impossible to remove without coming into contact with the cardboard. Move the cardboard so that it is not a concern for contacting the scoop.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. 

The tea maker has duck tape being used as a repair on the surface behind the where the jug sits. This is located on top of the ice machine and next to a hand washing sink. Tape is generally not a good repair option near food or moisture surfaces. The location was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x3) 4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The walk-in freezer fan cover has an accumulation of dust with pieces that appear to be ready to fly off. This is a repeat violation from the inspections conducted on 3/6/23, 9/20/23 and 12/29/23. Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to routinely clean this area. Correct by next routine inspection.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-305.11: (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions. 

An employee phone is observed on the shelf above the sandwich prep station. Education was conducted and the phone removed to correct. Store employee belongings away from food preparation and/or contact surfaces.
